bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar plans nine jaggery units in Muzaffarpur to support sugarcane farmers - ChiniMandi
bihar_raw_news.content: All News English Indian Sugar News Sugar News Top News Trendings AI Representational Image Muzaffarpur: Sugarcane farmers in Muzaffarpur may soon have a local avenue to process and market their produce, as the Bihar government plans to establish jaggery-making units in the district under its Fourth Agriculture Roadmap, Jagran reported. Muzaffarpur has been selected under the Bihar State Jaggery Industry Promotion Programme, with a proposal to establish nine jaggery production units in the district. The initiative is aimed at providing farmers in areas located away from sugar mills with a local market for their sugarcane while creating an additional source of income. Of the proposed units, six will be allocated under the general category and three under the Scheduled Caste category. A total of nine farmers or entrepreneurs are expected to benefit from the scheme, with financial assistance provided by the government for setting up the units. The programme specifically seeks to support sugarcane growers in non-milling areas by creating local processing facilities, reducing their dependence on sugar mills and markets in other districts. Subsidy of up to 50% Depending on production and crushing capacity, jaggery units can be established at an investment ranging from ₹12 lakh to ₹1 crore. Farmers or entrepreneurs will be eligible for a government subsidy of up to 50% of the project cost under the scheme. The financial support is expected to encourage entrepreneurs to establish jaggery-processing facilities at both small and larger scales. Local processing to reduce transportation difficulties Farmers living far from sugar mills currently face difficulties in disposing of their sugarcane and may have to depend on markets in other areas. The proposed local jaggery units are expected to reduce these challenges by allowing growers to process sugarcane into jaggery and sell the finished product in local markets. The initiative is also expected to create additional income and employment opportunities in rural areas. Production licence mandatory Farmers will have to obtain a production licence before starting a jaggery manufacturing unit. Assistant Cane Director Arvind Kumar Ravi said applicants would have to submit their applications to the office of the District Cane Development Officer. Applicants will be required to deposit a ₹2,100 challan for the licence. The application will then be forwarded by the district authorities to the directorate. Farmers will be able to apply for a jaggery unit only after receiving the licence. Online applications underway The online application process for the scheme has already begun. Interested farmers can apply to avail themselves of the benefits. The department expects the expansion of local jaggery production to help increase sugarcane farmers’ incomes while generating new employment opportunities in rural areas.

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar floods: Rahul Gandhi urges govt to carry out relief, rescue operations with full promptness
bihar_raw_news.content: PTI File Photo: Rahul Gandhi urges swift relief as devastating Bihar floods affect nearly 50 lakh people across 15 districts. New Delhi: In the wake of devastating floods in Bihar, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday urged the government and the administration to carry out relief and rescue operations with full promptness and ensure that essential aid reaches the affected families as soon as possible. The Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha also appealed to Congress workers to step forward and provide all possible assistance to the affected people. "The loss of lives due to the devastating floods in Bihar is extremely heartbreaking. I express my deepest condolences to the families who have lost their loved ones in this disaster. My sympathies are with all those affected by this tragedy," Gandhi said in a post in Hindi on X. "I appeal to Congress workers to step forward and provide all possible assistance to the affected people. At the same time, I expect the government and administration to carry out relief and rescue operations with full promptness and ensure that essential aid reaches the affected families as soon as possible," Gandhi said. The state has recorded 112.7 mm of rain so far in September, around six per cent above normal, the local weather office said. Read more: Bihar flood situation grim, over 47 lakh affected across 15 districts An official said incessant rain in the catchment areas of rivers flowing from Nepal into Bihar, coupled with heavy rainfall, has caused several rivers and streams to flow above their danger marks. According to the Disaster Management Department, 49.67 lakh people in 15 districts have been affected by floods. The affected districts are Patna, Bhojpur, Saran, Vaishali, Bhagalpur, Begusarai, Buxar, Samastipur, Munger, Katihar, Lakhisarai, Khagaria, Purnea, Madhepura and Araria. bihar_raw_news.title: SJVN CMD Marks Buxar Unit-II Commercial Launch - HIMACHAL HEADLINES
bihar_raw_news.content: NEWS September 15, 2026 admin Bhupender Gupta, Chairman & Managing Director, SJVN, inaugurated a program organized at project premises to commemorate significant milestone of commercial operation of Unit-II (660 MW) of 1320 MW Buxar Thermal Power Project (BTPP) in Bihar. Sh. Rajesh Kumar Chandel, Director (Projects), SJVN, was also present on the occasion. Sh. Bhupender Gupta marked the occasion by cutting the ribbon and pressing the ceremonial inauguration button. He also inaugurated the Centralized Control Room of the Project and visited key operational components, including the Ash Dyke, to take stock of operational preparedness and functioning. Addressing Team STPL, Sh. Bhupender Gupta congratulated entire team on the achievement and attributed the milestone to their collective efforts, dedication and teamwork. Highlighting the strategic importance, Sh. Gupta stated that project will play an important role in meeting the energy requirements of Bihar and supporting socio-economic development of the state. He called upon Team STPL to maintain the momentum and focus on safe, efficient and reliable operation of the power plant. Sh. Bhupender Gupta and Sh. Rajesh Kumar Chandel were accorded a warm welcome by Sh. Pulak Kumar Mukhopadhyay, Chief Executive Officer, SJVN Thermal Private Limited (STPL), along with senior officials of STPL. On this occasion, Sh. Rajesh Kumar Chandel, Director (Projects) appreciated the commitment and sustained efforts of Team STPL and credited the achievement to strong team spirit of everyone associated with the project. During the visit, Sh. Bhupender Gupta and Sh. Rajesh Kumar Chandel also met Sh. Ajay Yadav, Secretary (Energy), Government of Bihar and Smt. Sahila, District Magistrate, Buxar. During the meeting, detailed discussions was held on various issues related to project including land acquisition works, CSR, PSP projects, PPA-related issues, renewable power available with SJVN and potential investment opportunities in Bihar. Underscoring SJVN’s commitment to environmental conservation, Sh. Bhupender Gupta and Sh. Rajesh Kumar Chandel also planted saplings at the Project premises. The 1320 MW Buxar Thermal Power Project, located at Chausa in Buxar District, Bihar, has been implemented by SJVN Thermal Private Limited (STPL), a wholly owned subsidiary of SJVN.

bihar_raw_news.title: 'Ensure 75% attendance at all times': Bihar CM Samrat Chaudhary's diktat to colleges
bihar_raw_news.content: 'Ensure 75% attendance at all times': Bihar CM Samrat Chaudhary's diktat to colleges Ensure that 75 per cent of students attend your college under all circumstances so that you can teach them,” the CM said, Join Our WhatsApp Channel Business Today Desk Updated Sep 15, 2026 11:17 AM IST Bihar CM Samrat Chaudhary Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary has directed newly appointed assistant professors to ensure at least 75% student attendance in the state’s newly opened degree colleges, warning that infrastructure expansion alone will not improve higher education outcomes without regular class participation. Addressing an orientation programme for 2,451 newly appointed assistant professors across 211 new degree colleges at Bapu Sabhagar in Patna on Sunday (September 13), Choudhary stressed that attendance is critical to making the government’s higher education push meaningful. Advertisement Read More MUST READ: 'Historic opportunity for youth': Bihar govt opens recruitment for 32,388 teachers “Until children come and study in your colleges, the importance of that college will not be realised. Ensure that 75 per cent of students attend your college under all circumstances so that you can teach them,” the CM said, according to ANI. He said the expansion of degree colleges would help students pursue higher education closer to their homes. “Today, around 8 to 10 lakh children from Bihar are still going outside the state to study,” he said, adding that the expansion of degree colleges would provide students an opportunity to pursue higher education closer to their homes. 211 colleges, 2,451 appointments in a day Choudhary highlighted that Bihar has become the first state in India to launch 211 state-run degree colleges on a single day, calling it a historic milestone in higher education. Alongside this, the state has appointed 2,451 assistant professors to staff these institutions, marking a major expansion of teaching capacity. Advertisement The Chief Minister said quality education and academic expansion will give a new direction to Bihar’s youth, and urged faculty to work with full dedication as they carry the “vital responsibility” of shaping the future of the state’s students. Professors to receive global training In a related announcement, Choudhary said around 100 of the newly appointed assistant professors will be sent to Oxford University and other top global institutions for one-month specialised training, with the state government bearing the entire cost. The initiative aims to expose teachers to modern teaching methods and boost their professional capabilities. On attendance, the CM said monitoring mechanisms would be strengthened to ensure students attend college regularly, adding that improved attendance is essential for the wider higher education reforms to succeed. national_raw_news.content: The government has announced that banks cannot impose any charges on Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions of up to 2,000 rupees. According to a government gazette notification no charges can be imposed on such 2,000 rupees payments made through RuPay-powered debit cards either. The notification said no bank or system provider can impose any direct or indirect charge on a person making or receiving payments through these modes. The Finance Ministry notified the changes under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act to clarify the rules around charges on UPI transactions. The notification specifically categorised RuPay-powered debit cards and UPI transactions of up to 2,000 rupees as “electronic modes of payment”. Last month, the government clarified that consumers will not be charged for making payments through the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), while any future merchant discount rate (MDR) will be limited to select transactions above a specified threshold. The Finance Ministry said that all person-to-person (P2P) UPI transactions will continue to remain free and there will be no blanket MDR on merchants. The government further added that such charges would be significantly lower than the MDR applicable to debit or credit card transactions. The clarification comes amid debate over a recent amendment to the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, with concerns being raised about the possibility of charges being imposed on UPI users.

national_raw_news.title: 54 mins ago | National 32 World Circular Economy Forum 2026 to begin today at Gandhinagar in Gujarat
national_raw_news.content: The prestigious ‘World Circular Economy Forum (WCEF) 2026’ is set to begin today at Mahatma Mandir in Gandhinagar, Gujarat. The conference which is being held for the first time in South Asia, will be jointly inaugurated by Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Bhupender Yadav and Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel. Held under the theme ‘Circular Economy: Transition for People and Prosperity,’ the event will gather over 2,000 stakeholders from more than 65 countries. The stage is set at Mahatma Mandir in Gandhinagar for the World Circular Economy Forum 2026, marking a major milestone in promoting sustainable economic transitions across South Asia. The forum aims to drive global circularity by emphasising the reuse, refurbishing, and recycling of materials to reintegrate them as valuable economic resources. Across the two days, the forum will host 4 plenary sessions and 16 thematic sessions covering key areas such as the application of AI, green energy, sustainable finance, governance, and the start-up ecosystem. Additionally, an international expo featuring over 125 exhibitors will showcase innovative, practical solutions for circular business models. The global event is jointly organised by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Central Pollution Control Board, Finnish Innovation Fund Sitra, and the Government of Gujarat. Union Minister of State for Environment Kirti Vardhan Singh and Finland’s Environment Minister Sari Multala will grace the valedictory session tomorrow, which will be followed by 80 accelerator sessions hosted globally on September 17th and 18th.

national_raw_news.title: 56 mins ago | National 39 CJI Surya Kant calls mechanism to address complaints against judges robust and timely
national_raw_news.content: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant has described the mechanism developed by the Supreme Court and high courts to address complaints against judges as robust, very responsive and timely, while stressing the need for continuous reform and greater transparency in the judiciary. Delivering the keynote address at the 6th Ram Jethmalani Memorial Lecture on Justice Seen to Be Done: Transparency and Public Trust as Pillars of the Legal System, in New Delhi yesterday, the CJI said reform must remain the norm and no institution could afford to take pride in remaining static. He said the judiciary itself had acknowledged the importance of criticism, reiterating the Supreme Court’s position that the institution is not, and cannot be, averse to criticism. He added fair, informed and constructive critique of judicial functioning is a legitimate and necessary feature of a vibrant constitutional democracy. Justice Surya Kant said this principle was at the heart of judicial transparency. He observed a court, cannot expect to command public confidence by placing itself beyond scrutiny. Instead, it must remain open to being examined, questioned and, where necessary, criticised. He also drew a distinction between public trust and public approval, saying true public trust is established when even those who lose a case continue to believe that the judicial process was fair.

national_raw_news.title: Pension Sakhis to take retirement security to doorstep of rural India - ANI News
national_raw_news.content: Pension Sakhis to take retirement security to doorstep of rural India Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Pension Sakhis to take retirement security to doorstep of rural India ANI | Updated: Sep 15, 2026 10:40 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], September 15 (ANI): In a major step towards taking pension awareness and retirement security to rural households, the Department of Rural Development (DoRD) and the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) today signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to create and support a community-based outreach mechanism of ‘Pension Sakhis’ across rural India. According to the Ministry of Rural Development, the MoU was signed between Amit Shukla, Joint Secretary, DoRD, and Sumeet Kaur Kapoor, Executive Director, PFRDA, in the presence of Rohit Kansal, Secretary, Department of Rural Development. The partnership seeks to leverage the extensive community institutional network created under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana: National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM), including its Banking Correspondent (BC) Sakhis and other trained community resource persons, to take pension awareness, financial literacy, enrolment and post-enrolment support closer to rural households. The initiative will seek to use the strength of the women-led SHG institutional architecture to address a fundamental challenge in pension coverage: reaching households that may have limited access to formal financial advice and retirement-planning services. Under the partnership, Pension Sakhis will act as trusted community-level facilitators, particularly reaching SHG members, rural women, Lakhpati Didis and other rural participants. They will support households with information on pension and retirement planning, facilitate enrolment, and provide assistance in understanding pension-related services. Speaking on the occasion, Rohit Kansal, Secretary, Department of Rural Development, said that rural households participating in the SHG movement have distinctive savings patterns, livelihood cycles and risk profiles, and that social security must therefore become an important part of the Mission’s larger objective of sustainable prosperity. He emphasised that “social security is not only about protection against vulnerability; it is also about giving households the confidence and resilience to pursue sustained economic advancement.” Kansal stressed that pension awareness and financial literacy must be built on honesty, transparency and trust. He further highlighted the importance of ensuring that rural citizens receive clear and transparent information so that they can make informed choices about their long-term financial security. Mamta Shankar highlighted the growing importance of retirement planning in the context of rising life expectancy and changing demographic patterns. She expressed the hope that the partnership would substantially improve awareness and adoption of pension products, including the National Pension System (NPS), among rural households that remain outside formal retirement and social-security mechanisms. The collaboration will also strengthen monitoring of outreach and enrolment through digital dashboards and mobile- and web-based solutions, including the Department’s own LoKoS system, enabling the participating institutions to track progress and identify gaps in coverage. Community-level outreach will be supported by appropriate digital systems for monitoring and service delivery. The MoU brings together two complementary strengths: PFRDA’s expertise in pension regulation and retirement-security systems and DAY-NRLM’s unparalleled community reach through women’s collectives...

national_raw_news.title: PIB Srinagar media delegation visits Dakshina Chitra Heritage Museum - Rising Kashmir
national_raw_news.content: PIB Srinagar media delegation visits Dakshina Chitra Heritage Museum Advertisment Breaking News Jammu and Kashmir News PIB Srinagar media delegation visits Dakshina Chitra Heritage Museum RK News 15 Sep 2026 07:28 IST Follow Us Chennai, Sep 14: A 13 member media delegation from Jammu and Kashmir, organised by Press Information Bureau (PIB), Srinagar, visited Dakshina Chitra Heritage Museum at Muttukadu, Tamil Nadu, on Monday as part of press tour being conducted by PIB Srinagar from Sep 13 to 19. The delegation was briefed about the museum and its heritage structures by curator Lakuma Chebrolu. She explained the architectural features of the traditional homes preserved at the museum and provided information about the different regional styles represented there. The museum houses reconstructed traditional heritage homes from Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Kerala. The delegation was informed that the houses were carefully dismantled and reconstructed at the site with the involvement of regional artisans and traditional master builders. The visiting media delegation also explored the traditional streetscapes and living environments recreated at the museum, providing an insight into the architectural and cultural traditions of the southern states. Sharath Nambiar, Director, Dakshina Chitra, interacted with the delegation and briefed them about the history of the museum and its role in preserving India's tangible and intangible cultural heritage. He also highlighted the support extended by the Government, particularly the Ministry of Culture, which provided land for the institution and continues to extend assistance from time to time. The visit provided the media delegation an opportunity to understand the preservation and presentation of traditional architecture, indigenous crafts and performing arts, and their relevance for contemporary audiences. Later the delegation also met Sanjay Ghosh, Deputy Director, CBFC Chennai. The delegation is led by Shahid Mohammad Lone, Field Publicity Officer (FPO), Central Bureau of Communication (CBC), serving as the Conducting Officer, with Ifham Ul Islam Information Assistant, PIB Srinagar accompanying the delegation. The media tour of Srinagar based journalists is also significant since Jammu and Kashmir and Tamil Nadu are states paired together under Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat (EBSB). Daily Excelsior 04:18 AM Sep 15, 2026 IST Journalists from Jammu posing for a group photograph during their Bhopal tour on Monday. Excelsior Correspondent BHOPAL, Sept 14: A 10-member media delegation from Jammu began a press tour of Madhya Pradesh with visits to two of the state's important archaeological and cultural heritage sites, the historic Siva Temple at Bhojpur and the prehistoric rock shelters of Bhimbetka. On the first day of the tour, the journalists visited the Siva Temple at Bhojpur, where they were briefed by officials accompanying the delegation on the history and architectural significance of the monument. Advertisement The delegation was also briefed on the temple's unique architectural features, including its massive stone construction and the scale of the structure. Officials explained the historical importance of the site and efforts to preserve the monument as part of the region's archaeological heritage. The journalists later proceeded to Bhimbetka, one of India's most important prehistoric archaeological sites and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Officials explained that the archaeological evidence at Bhimbetka spans a very long period of human history, with the site offering insights into the development of human culture and artistic expression. The delegation's visit to both sites provided the journalists with an opportunity to understand Madhya Pradesh's rich archaeological heritage beyond written accounts and photographs. The tour has been organized by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Jammu, to provide journalists with an opportunity to experience the cultural, historical and developmental landscape of Madhya Pradesh firsthand. national_raw_news.title: SKUAST‑K scholar brings national recognition at NBEC-2026, Bengaluru - Rising Kashmir
national_raw_news.content: SKUAST‑K scholar brings national recognition at NBEC-2026, Bengaluru Advertisment Breaking News City SKUAST‑K scholar brings national recognition at NBEC-2026, Bengaluru RK News 14 Sep 2026 07:30 IST Follow Us Srinagar, Sep 13: In a landmark achievement for SKUAST‑K, Bushra Naaz, PhD scholar under the mentorship of Dr. Ajaz Ahmed Malik, Head, KVK, Ganderbal has been declared a winner at the National Bio Entrepreneurship Competition (NBEC) 2026, held in Bengaluru. The 2026 edition received an overwhelming response, with over 3,200 registrations from 34 States and Union Territories, making it one of the most competitive national platforms for science-driven entrepreneurship. After successive rounds of screening, mentoring, pitching, and evaluation on parameters such as scientific validity, novelty, feasibility, business potential, team strength, and clarity of articulation, only the most promising student advanced to the Grand Finale. Her pioneering research on plant-based meat analogues stood out for its scientific depth, translational potential, and entrepreneurial promise. In recognition of this breakthrough, Bushra Naaz received a ₹1 lakh award, presented in the presence of Dr. Kiran Mazumdar Shaw, Executive Chairperson of Biocon, and other eminent figures from India’s biotechnology ecosystem. Reflecting on the achievement, Dr. Ajaz Ahmed Malik, Head KVK, Ganderbal and Major Advisor to Bushra Naaz, remarked. The recognition of this work is deeply gratifying. For over a decade, I have been engaged with the scientific potential of fava bean, and it is inspiring to see this line of research now being advanced by my student into an innovative solution with societal and commercial relevance. Vice Chancellor SKUAST-K Prof. Nazir Ahmad Ganai congratulated both Bushra Naaz and Dr. Ajaz Malik, stating: This achievement is a proud moment for SKUAST‑K and aligns with our vision to be counted among the top universities in the country. It exemplifies how our scholars and faculty are not only contributing to academic excellence but also translating research into innovation and entrepreneurship. Such recognitions strengthen our resolve to position SKUAST‑K at the forefront of national and global scientific leadership. Read More Subscribe to our Newsletter!
